look_here_first: Tall nearly glabrous dioecious amaranth with long-petioled leaves and long terminal spikes; pistillate plants have sharp bracts longer than the tepals.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pistillate bracts 4–6 mm and longer than tepals

lookalikes.differences: Tall, smooth, dioecious Palmer contrasts with hairy monoecious redroot pigweed. No paired nodal spines.
